0.0.n: This noun praises the achievement that made Kawasaki the game's hero.

0.1.n: Links the outstanding contribution to Kawasaki, describing him as the player responsible.

0.2.n: This is the player's family name.

1.0.n: Combines with 終了 to refer to the game ending.

1.1.n: This noun combines with 試合 to mean the end of the game.

1.2.n: Follows 試合終了 to specify when the interview happened.

1.4.n: Names the feeling that has not yet subsided; the subject marker が is omitted here.

1.5.n: A literary expression from 冷める, with やらぬ indicating that the fading has not fully happened.

1.6.n: Refers to the surrounding situation, not a physical location.

2.1.n: Connects NHK to the interview, identifying the broadcaster conducting it.

2.2.n: A borrowed English word used as a noun.

2.3.n: Marks the interview as what he responded to.

2.4.n: Polite past form of 答える; インタビューに答える means to answer an interviewer's questions.

3.0.n: The family name comes before the given name 宗則 in Japanese.

3.1.n: 宗 is the first character of the given name 宗則, Munenori, not a separate word here.

3.2.n: 則 is the second character of the given name 宗則, Munenori, not a separate word here.

3.3.n: Added after an athlete's name as a respectful title.

3.4.n: Marks Kawasaki as the person whose visit the speaker gratefully received.

3.5.n: A respectful form referring to someone's visit, used here with いただく.

3.6.n: Polite past form of humble いただく; with お越し, it expresses appreciation for the guest's visit.

4.0.n: Praises the player's performance; what was magnificent is understood from context.

4.1.n: でし is the part of polite です used before the past ending た.

4.2.n: Completes でした, making the praise refer to the performance just finished.

0.tip: 殊勲の川崎 is a compact news-style description identifying Kawasaki as the player who made the outstanding contribution.

1.lit: Immediately after the game's end, amid excitement not yet subsided,
1.tip: 冷めやらぬ describes excitement that still lingers and gives the narration a formal, literary tone.

2.tip: インタビューに答える means to answer questions in an interview, with に marking what is being responded to.

3.lit: We received the coming of player Kawasaki Munenori.
3.tip: お越しいただきました is a very polite way for a host to say that a guest has joined them.

4.tip: でした is the polite past form of です; Japanese leaves out the subject when it is clear.
